title: Yod Keret
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Kiddushin 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.16b.15), Rav Yosef said, “I see Yod Keret here.” The [Arukh](https://torahwords.org/aru_1497) cites the explanation that this is the name of a sage, while [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Kiddushin.16b.15.1) explains it differently.

notes.text: The consulted Kiddushin explicitly names Rav Yosef, resolving the initials in Hyman’s source. The phrase בע״א in the supplied notice means that Rashi explains it differently.

[Ritva](https://www.sefaria.org/Ritva_on_Kiddushin.16b.6) gives Rav Yosef as Rashi’s reading and attributes the reading Rabbah to Raavad. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1802&lang=en) records the two interpretations and the different names.

Kiddushin 16b names Rav Yosef, resolving the initials in the earlier note. Rashi explains the image as turning a small yod into a large city, a figure for lengthening a teaching needlessly. The Arukh gives this explanation and also quotes a Gaon who takes Yod Keret as a sage’s name. The later Hafla’ah proposes reading “city” for “sage.” Ritva gives Rav Yosef for Rashi’s reading and reports a different reading, Rabbah, from the Raavad, who takes Yod Keret as a person’s name.
